title: The Revakhanda of the Vayu Purana
author: vyasa
attributionNote: The Revākhaṇḍa that belongs to the Vāyupurāṇa tradition but was printed inside the Veṅkateśvara edition of the Skandapurāṇa, where it stood at the head of that Purana's Revākhaṇḍa. GRETIL follows the Veṅkateśvara Steam Press edition (Bombay 1910) and its reprints, and the file was input by Jürgen Neuss.
description: This Revākhaṇḍa is the older of the two Narmada Puranas: it tells how the river came to the earth, the pilgrimage to its banks and to the shrines of its valley, the greatness of Omkāreśvara and of the sage Kapila's hermitage, the gifts, fasts and baths the pilgrim undertakes, and the lineage of the royal houses that ruled the region. Much of its material on the sacred sites is shared with the Purana of the Vāyu tradition it belongs to.
historicalContext: The text's history is a case study in Puranic transmission: because the printer placed it inside the Skanda Purāṇa, later catalogues counted it as that Purana's own Revākhaṇḍa, and only the comparison of the manuscripts showed that it is the Vāyu Purāṇa's. GRETIL publishes it under that finding.
availabilityNote: Complete as GRETIL publishes it: 232 chapters and 7,776 verses, streamed from GRETIL at read time. Each passage is one verse, addressed as chapter.verse. The library holds the Skandapurāṇa's own Revākhaṇḍa as a separate work, and the two are read side by side.
